name: Josiah
description: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: He prophesies that a child named Josiah, of the house of David, will one day burn the false priests of the high places on that very altar and burn men's bones upon it.

note.label: 1 Kings 13: The Man of God and the Two Prophets

points: His own servants conspire against him and slay him in his house; the people of the land slay the conspirators and make Josiah his son king in his stead.

note.label: 2 Kings 21: The Wickedness of Manasseh and Amon

points: Josiah begins to reign at eight years old and reigns thirty-one years, doing that which is right in the sight of the Most High and walking in all the way of David, turning neither to the right nor the left.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

points: Josiah also took away all the houses of the high places in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel had made to provoke the Lord to anger, and did to them as he had done at Bethel.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

points: Josiah also put away the workers with familiar spirits, the wizards, the images, the idols, and all the abominations spied in Judah and Jerusalem, that he might perform the words of the law found by Hilkiah.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

points: Josiah got involved in a matter that did not concern him and lost his life in it, a warning not to enter into quarrels that are not one's own.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

points: Pharaohnechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates, and Josiah went against him and was slain at Megiddo.

note.label: 2 Kings 23: Josiah Reads the Law and Cleanses the Land

points: Josiah had four sons: Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah and Shallum; Jehoiakim's son Jeconiah is the Jehoiachin of Kings and the Jechonias of Matthew.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: The people of the land slay the conspirators and make Josiah his son king in his stead. A sentence not executed speedily set his heart to do more evil, and his sins abounded to his own destruction.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

points: Comparing the ages shows the point: Manasseh began at twelve, Amon at twenty two, and Josiah at eight, yet the youngest was the wisest. Better is a poor and wise child than an old and foolish king who will no more be admonished.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

points: Josiah takes away all the abominations out of all the countries belonging to the children of Israel and makes all present serve the Lord their God, and they depart not from following him all his days. All wisdom is the performance of the law.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 34: Josiah the Wise Child Finds the Book of the Law

points: Josiah keeps a Passover unto the Lord in Jerusalem, and they kill the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, keeping the laws pertaining to the Passover.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 35: Josiah Keeps the Passover

points: Josiah gives the people thirty thousand lambs and kids and three thousand bullocks for the Passover offerings, and his princes give willingly to the people, the priests, and the Levites.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 35: Josiah Keeps the Passover

points: All the service of the Lord is prepared the same day to keep the Passover and offer burnt offerings on the altar according to the commandment of king Josiah.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 35: Josiah Keeps the Passover

points: The children of Israel present keep the Passover and the feast of unleavened bread seven days, and there was no Passover like it kept in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet; none of the kings of Israel kept such a Passover as Josiah kept in his eighteenth year.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 35: Josiah Keeps the Passover

points: After this, Necho king of Egypt comes up to fight at Carchemish by Euphrates, and Josiah goes out against him though Necho sends word that his war is not with Josiah and that God had commanded him to make haste.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 35: Josiah Keeps the Passover

points: Josiah will not turn his face but disguises himself to fight, hearkening not to the words of Necho from the mouth of God, and the archers shoot him in the valley of Megiddo.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 35: Josiah Keeps the Passover

points: His servants take him from the chariot and bring him to Jerusalem, where he dies and is buried, and all Judah and Jerusalem mourn, and Jeremiah laments for Josiah, written in the Lamentations, a book of the Bible.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 35: Josiah Keeps the Passover

points: The rest of the acts of Josiah and his goodness, according to that which is written in the law of the Lord, and his deeds first and last, are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 35: Josiah Keeps the Passover

points: The people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah and make him king in Jerusalem; he is twenty three years old and reigns three months.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

points: The words of Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah of the priests in Anathoth, came in the days of Josiah, through Jehoiakim, and to the end of Zedekiah, up to the carrying away of Jerusalem captive.

note.label: Jeremiah 1: The Prophet Ordained unto the Nations

points: In the days of Josiah the Most High saw that backsliding Israel had gone up upon every high mountain and under every green tree and played the harlot, and her treacherous sister Judah saw it.

note.label: Jeremiah 3: Backsliding Israel Called to Return

points: The people are told not to weep for the dead but to weep sore for him that goes away, Shallum the son of Josiah who reigned in his father's place.

note.label: Jeremiah 22: Woe to the Unrighteous Kings of Judah

points: The word came to Jeremiah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the first year of Nebuchadnezzar, recounting that for twenty-three years, from the thirteenth year of Josiah, the Most High had risen early and spoken but the people would not hearken.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the Most High tells Jeremiah to take a roll of a book and write in it all the words He has spoken against Israel, against Judah, and against all the nations, from the days of Josiah until that day.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: King Zedekiah the son of Josiah reigns in place of Coniah, whom Nebuchadnezzar made king in the land of Judah, but neither he nor his servants nor the people hearken to the words of the Most High spoken by Jeremiah.

note.label: Jeremiah 37: The Prophet Arrested and Imprisoned

points: This is the word Jeremiah spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah when he had written these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah.

note.label: Jeremiah 45: The Word of Comfort to Baruch the Scribe

points: The word of the Lord which came unto Zephaniah in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah.

note.label: Zephaniah 1: The Great Day of the Lord Is Near
